Frequency of occurrence per rank (the Buckland Table B1 layout)

Source: R/dv_explore.R
dv_fo_table.Rd

The classical frequency of occurrence (%FO): the proportion of non-empty stomachs that contain each taxon, computed INDEPENDENTLY at each taxonomic rank. Because a stomach can contain several categories, and because a parent's %FO is recomputed from stomach presence rather than summed from its children, these values are non-additive across ranks - which is exactly why they are reported as a nested hierarchy of levels (Buckland et al., 2017). This is distinct from the share of prey records in dv_build_tree() (pct_occ), which is additive so that it can be drawn as a sunburst: the two agree only where each stomach holds at most one record of the taxon, which rarely holds at coarse ranks. Stomach identifiers must be unique across predators (see dv_validate()).

Usage

dv_fo_table(prep, rank = NULL, by = NULL, include_na = TRUE)

Arguments

prep

A dietview_prep from dv_prepare().

rank

A single rank (e.g. "genus") or NULL for every rank stacked.

by

Optional covariate to compute %FO within each level of.

include_na

Keep the explicit unidentified category at each rank.

Value

A data.frame with (optional) by, rank, taxon, n_stomachs (stomachs containing the taxon), n_total (stomachs in the group), and pct_fo.

Examples

# the standard set-up: public ICES data, non-food items and nematodes dropped
phylum <- ices_lineage$phylum[match(ices_diet$prey_aphia_id, ices_lineage$prey_aphia_id)]
dat <- ices_diet[ices_diet$item_type != "non_food" & !phylum %in% "Nematoda", ]
spec <- dv_spec(
  predator       = "predator_common",
  predator_latin = "predator_latin",
  stomach        = "stomach_id",
  prey_id        = "prey_aphia_id",
  prey_name      = "prey_name",
  weight         = "prey_weight_g",
  count          = "prey_count",
  digestion      = "digestion_label",
  covariates     = c("region", "year", "quarter")
)
# Atlantic cod only, for speed
cod <- dat[dat$predator_common == "Atlantic cod", ]
prep_cod <- dv_prepare(cod, spec, taxonomy = "table", lineage = ices_lineage,
                       verbose = FALSE)
dv_fo_table(prep_cod, rank = "class")
#>     rank        taxon n_stomachs n_total pct_fo
#> 1  class Malacostraca        618     991  62.36
#> 2  class    Teleostei        332     991  33.50
#> 3  class           NA        323     991  32.59
#> 4  class   Polychaeta        136     991  13.72
#> 5  class  Ophiuroidea         49     991   4.94
#> 6  class     Bivalvia         28     991   2.83
#> 7  class   Gastropoda         18     991   1.82
#> 8  class  Cephalopoda         10     991   1.01
#> 9  class     Gephyrea          2     991   0.20
#> 10 class       Myxini          1     991   0.10
#> 11 class    Trematoda          1     991   0.10
